headline: pki.scep gains the SCEP HTTP client verbs (RFC 8894): getCACaps, getCACert, enroll, and renew drive a certificate enrollment against a SCEP CA over the shipped pkiMessage codec.
summary: The SCEP client codec (pki.scep.build / parse) now has the HTTP verbs that carry it to a CA. pki.scep.getCACaps reads a CA's advertised capabilities, pki.scep.getCACert retrieves the CA certificate pinned to an out-of-band fingerprint, and pki.scep.enroll and pki.scep.renew POST a PKCSReq or RenewalReq and read the CertRep, selecting the issued certificate by public-key match, throwing on a FAILURE with the CA's failInfo, and returning a PENDING for the caller to retry. The verbs run over an injectable transport (pki.transport.https by default), authenticate the CA response against the CA certificate, and require the response nonce to echo the request. The strong RFC 8894 profile is the default: content encryption is AES-128-CBC, the digest is SHA-256, and the GetCACaps response, which is unauthenticated, never lowers the client's algorithm choice. GetNextCACert, automatic polling, GetCert, GetCRL, GET-carried PKIOperation, and HTTP proxy authentication are not in this release.

Added: pki.scep.getCACaps(baseUrl, opts) queries a SCEP CA's advertised capabilities (RFC 8894 sec. 3.5) and returns the parsed keyword set; pki.scep.parseCapabilities(text) exposes the parser directly. The response is unauthenticated (sec. 7.5), so the verb reports what the CA claims without downgrading on it; pass expectSCEPStandard or requireStrongProfile to fail closed when the strong profile is absent.

pki.scep.getCACert(baseUrl, opts) retrieves the CA certificate, either a single DER certificate or a certs-only chain (RFC 8894 sec. 4.2). Pass an out-of-band expectedFingerprint (a hex string or Buffer, SHA-256 by default) and a returned certificate must match it or the response is refused (RFC 8894 sec. 2.2); omitting it returns the certificates for the caller to authenticate.

pki.scep.enroll(baseUrl, opts) and pki.scep.renew(baseUrl, opts) POST a PKCSReq or RenewalReq to ?operation=PKIOperation and read the CertRep. The response signature is authenticated against the CA certificate and its recipientNonce must echo the request's senderNonce; on SUCCESS the issued certificate is selected out of the response by SubjectPublicKeyInfo match, a FAILURE throws scep/enrollment-failed carrying the CA's failInfo, and a PENDING returns { status: "PENDING", transactionId } to retry. The content key is transported under RSAES-OAEP, so the CA certificate must be an RSA keyEncipherment certificate.
Fixed: The EST, SCEP, and ACME client verbs override the mTLS client certificate, key, and pinned servername on a cross-origin redirect rather than omitting them. A transport constructed with a default client credential (for example pki.transport.https({ tls: { cert, key } })) no longer presents that credential to the redirected origin.
